openings.claim: A broad resilient tapping face may lower the tile without concentrated edge loading: the pad is predicted to spread force across the face while repeated impulses move the bed.
openings.discriminator: Predicts fewer chips than a narrow face; relative adjustment time has no prediction. Any chip or persistent height mismatch defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed only: compare chip occurrence and height change on sacrificial matched bed conditions.
openings.uncertainty: Required pad stiffness and sensitivity to bed curing are unknown.

lineage.reason: Retains the force-spreading/impulse relation, comparison, both defeat conditions, time uncertainty, proposed probe, unknowns and declared preserves fit.

Declared conditional: warming before tapping might reduce required impulse through changed adhesive response permitting movement at lower loading. Predicts easier adjustment than broad-pad tapping only if adhesive responds reversibly to warmth; no impulse reduction defeats advantage. Proposed warmed-versus-ambient sacrificial-bed comparison requires explicit relaxation of no heating. Adhesive response and resulting bond integrity remain unknown; no thermal source is supplied.

Declared violates: frame-mounted static pressing might adjust height without repeated impacts through sustained distributed force predicted to move the bed gradually. Rejected because a fixed frame violates hand-held use. It might still chip; absent impacts do not establish safety. Probe is parked: a separate surrogate cracking study cannot establish in-case fit. Crack risk, required load and adjustment precision remain unresolved.

decision: Prioritize only the proposed D1 comparison for correcting a small height mismatch. Preserve no edge chipping, hand-held use and no adhesive heating; unknown resources authorize no relaxation. Tile/bed properties are unspecified and the resilient pad hypothetical. All proposals and predictions are synthetic: no real tile, adhesive, equipment or observed adequacy is supplied.
